result.request: Build a fresh pivot of simple-by-design in this directory: remove workflows, retain the semantic-boundary engine, design task solutions through adaptive loops that remove consequential uncertainty.
result.goal: A standalone skill that produces a justified solution design by repeatedly finding and resolving consequential uncertainty, without workflow selection or a fixed task sequence.
constraints: Original /home/joshsimon/Projects/pi-skills/simple-by-design stays unchanged.
Treat .agents/artifact/adaptive.md as the design brief; its conceptual plan workflow must not reintroduce workflows.
Preserve concrete pair/defeater witnesses, intent/fact/choice resolver separation, consequentiality gates, evidence provenance, and reopening on contradiction.
Designing a task solution does not grant permission to implement it; report-only and other task limits remain binding.
Generated Markdown belongs under .agents/artifacts/; no existing Git repository or implementation is present.
This design run cannot implement; obtain review/approval after its summary.
criteria: No workflow catalog, workflow loader, YAML steps, numbered task stages, or bounded rewind model.
Next work follows a surviving consequential witness or an explicit design acceptance check, not a mandatory checklist.
Unresolved intent is asked of the requester; facts require observations; engineering choices use established policy then simplest adequate design.
Durable state preserves questions, evidence, decisions, dependencies and revision history across interruption; unresolved blockers cannot be reported as complete.
Acceptance includes concrete counterexamples covering wrong resolver, weak criteria, revoked assumptions, false completion, scope violations, deferral, and resumption.
A straightforward unambiguous task can finish without manufactured questions or unnecessary cycles.

questions.question: Which revision does a recorded evaluation certify, given that recording it changes the event-log revision?
questions.witness: If current revision includes the evaluation event, each evaluation is instantly stale; accepting any earlier revision permits obsolete review to justify a changed design.

questions.question: How does contradictory evidence after completion reopen the same task without erasing history or expanding authority?
questions.witness: A terminal complete flag can reject needed reopening; unrestricted later edits can preserve a now-unjustified complete status or silently turn the design task into new work.

questions.question: Which existing behavior is the semantic-boundary engine, and which code is workflow orchestration?
questions.witness: Copying the Python runner retains workflow selection and bounded rewind; retaining only prose without its resolver and reopening rules loses consequential-boundary behavior.

questions.question: What outcome and authority should the new adaptive loop have?
questions.witness: A solution-design loop and an implementation executor can both resemble the artifact, but the latter can edit task files before the user has authorized implementation.

questions.question: What is the smallest durable runtime that supports adaptive questions without becoming another workflow engine?
questions.witness: A single fixed plan workflow still prescribes task stages; an entirely transient prompt cannot preserve unresolved questions or evidence after interruption.

questions.question: How are questions settled, deferred, reopened, and invalidated without washing away evidence?
questions.witness: Latest-result overwrite can hide contradictions; marking an intent question resolved with the agent's guess can make an unsupported design appear complete.

questions.question: What controls completion, independent evaluation, and unproductive loops?
questions.witness: An empty question ledger can pass despite weak criteria or unexamined assumptions; a fixed retry cap can label unfinished work complete; evaluator absence can masquerade as independent review.

questions.question: What evidence would demonstrate that the pivot preserves semantic behavior instead of only passing structural state tests?
questions.witness: A CLI can reject malformed JSON while its instructions still cause fabricated intent, needless questions, or scope violations.

decisions.question: What is the smallest durable runtime?
decisions.answer: Use a stdlib-only Python CLI with new/show/record/finish operations and per-task state at .agents/sbd-adaptive/<task-id>.json. The agent chooses the next warranted observation, clarification, decision or design update; no stages are scheduled. Separate CLI adaptation, pure ledger validation/projection, and atomic persistence. Each state document holds schema version plus an ordered immutable event history; derive the current view rather than storing a second authoritative ledger. Writers lock, require an expected revision, validate before append and atomically replace the document. Task IDs cannot escape the state directory. No automatic restart or cross-task inheritance.
decisions.rationale: The brief requires interruption-safe history, while the explicit pivot removes predefined processes. The smallest runtime stores and validates facts about progress without choosing cognitive work.

evidence.shows: Adaptive next work, persistent question ledger, history rather than overwrite.
One owner, plain data and explicit boundaries.

decisions.question: How do uncertainty and evidence evolve?
decisions.answer: Questions contain stable id, text, intent/fact/choice type, structured witness, consequence, dependencies, resolver and next resolving action. Record observations, answers, provisional choices, deferrals, contradictions and design revisions as new events. Intent answers cite the requester or authoritative requester documents; fact answers cite observations; choice answers cite policy/source precedence and rationale, with viable alternatives, tradeoff and revisit when consequential. Inference/unknown never become observed evidence by relabeling a status. Provisional fact/choice answers require cheap reversal, detectability and a revisit condition. Deferral names its boundary, owner/reason and trigger; it cannot hide a requirement for the current design. Reopening or replacing relied-on evidence/answers transitively invalidates dependent answers, design checks and evaluations. History remains available.
decisions.rationale: A question's status is not evidence. Dependency invalidation and typed resolution preserve the old engine's core distinctions through adaptive cycles.

evidence.shows: Resolver separation, reversible assumptions, dependency reopening.
Evidence provenance, established versus assumed basis, consequential decision metadata.

alternatives.option: Latest answer wins without dependency invalidation
alternatives.rejected_because: Leaves downstream conclusions apparently valid after their basis changes.

alternatives.rejected_because: Discards legitimate implementation freedom and safe explicit deferral.

decisions.tradeoff: Record only relied-on dependencies and consequential questions; irrelevant uncertainty is not made into mandatory ledger work. Runtime validates claimed provenance structure but cannot authenticate it.
decisions.revisit: Behavioral evaluation finds a material wrong-resolver resolution, hidden deferral or missed dependent reopening.

decisions.question: What makes the evaluator and termination trustworthy?
decisions.answer: Evaluate the current request, permissions, evidence, decisions and candidate design, not merely the planner's narrative or the open-question count. Return only concrete surviving pairs, defeaters or failed required checks; separate discovery from answering. Questions about goal, assumptions, alternatives, authority, evidence and omissions are optional probes, not six mandatory stages. Before completion require a current candidate design, all required design acceptance checks supported, no unresolved required question, valid dependencies and a challenge tied to the exact pre-completion snapshot, atomically accepted with completion as specified in D7. A fresh independent reviewer reads an immutable state snapshot when available; otherwise record local-only evaluation explicitly, never claim independence, and block if independent review is required. When no authorized action can obtain progress, pause as blocked with the needed resolver; never convert a retry/token limit into success.
decisions.rationale: The brief explicitly distinguishes an independent evaluator from proof and requires observable justification and permission compliance.

evidence.shows: Optional evaluation questions, independent challenge, acceptance evidence, no manufactured uncertainty.
Only add instructions that change identifiable decisions.

decisions.question: How will the pivot be evaluated?
decisions.answer: Separate deterministic ledger tests from agent-behavior evaluation. Test schema rejection, resolver/evidence shape, IDs, dependencies/cycles, reopen propagation, safe deferral, stale evaluations, expected revisions, locking, atomic write failure, corrupt state, CLI resume, history and completion refusal. Add semantic cases for feature design, behavior-preserving refactor, intermittent incident investigation, architectural tradeoff, security evidence, clarification-only tasks and precise negative controls. For each record the witness, chosen resolver, action/decision changed, unnecessary questions, scope compliance and assurance limit. Use at least one held-out task; do not claim behavioral improvement from fixtures or unexecuted evaluations. Port only evidence policies a concrete scenario needs, not five domain workflows or a language-reference catalog.
decisions.rationale: Structural validation cannot demonstrate that the instruction changes real agent decisions, and unambiguous tasks must not pay for unnecessary loops.

evidence.shows: Retain evidence standards, test comparison quality and cost, avoid forced questions.
Observable behavioral outcomes and unfamiliar-case robustness.

alternatives.option: Unit tests alone establish semantic preservation
alternatives.rejected_because: They can validate state while instructions still encourage unsupported decisions.

alternatives.rejected_because: Adds unproven process and hides the greenfield pivot under old workflow content.

decisions.tradeoff: A first release can establish deterministic correctness and report limited behavioral evidence; it must not claim universal completeness or full legacy-workflow equivalence.
decisions.revisit: A held-out case finds a distinct consequential failure not caught by the current semantic contract.

decisions.question: Which revision does final evaluation certify?
decisions.answer: The evaluator certifies the immutable ledger snapshot at revision R. finish --at R accepts that evaluation and appends its completion record together in one locked atomic transition only while the ledger head is still R. The resulting event is R+1 and explicitly certifies its parent R; it does not require evaluating itself. Any intervening record makes the submission stale. Non-final evaluation findings may be recorded normally, but cannot be reused to finish a later revision.
decisions.rationale: One expected revision and a combined final-evaluation/completion event avoids both a self-invalidating review and stale-review acceptance.

evidence.shows: Prefer the smallest conventional adequate solution and one state owner.

evidence.ref: Inline challenge counterexample, design run 1 attempt 1
evidence.shows: Appending a separate evaluation changes the head revision; an atomic parent-revision contract removes the ambiguity.

alternatives.option: Separate content and metadata revision counters
alternatives.rejected_because: Adds another invalidation concept without a present need.

alternatives.option: Accept an evaluation of any earlier revision
alternatives.rejected_because: Permits obsolete evidence to justify a changed design.

decisions.tradeoff: An unrelated intervening ledger record also requires re-evaluation; conservative freshness is preferable to extra version machinery at this scale.
decisions.revisit: Measured re-evaluation cost demonstrates a need to distinguish substantive changes from annotations.

decisions.question: How does new evidence reopen a completed task?
decisions.answer: After completion, reject ordinary mutations until an explicit reopen event cites the contradictory observation or reached revisit condition and names affected records. Append that event to the same history, invalidate affected dependents and prior completion, and return the same original design request to active status. Prior completion remains historical, never erased. Reopening grants no new authority. A materially different goal is a new task; changed intent or permissions must be sourced to the requester rather than inferred from reopening.
decisions.rationale: Revisiting a justified decision is distinct from silently modifying completed work or restarting a request.

evidence.shows: Reopen affected work on contradiction or revisit condition.
Preserve history instead of overwriting retries.
An explicit reopening event is sufficient without a restart mechanism.

alternatives.option: Completed tasks are permanently immutable
alternatives.rejected_because: Cannot honor reopening when relied-on evidence is contradicted.

alternatives.option: Allow ordinary edits while preserving complete status
alternatives.rejected_because: Completion may outlive its evidence or conceal scope expansion.

decisions.tradeoff: Reopening requires an explicit causal record; it preserves auditability without promising that all external contradictions can be detected automatically.
decisions.revisit: A real scope revision cannot be represented safely as either a requester-sourced revision or a separate task.

current.answer: The evaluator certifies the immutable ledger snapshot at revision R. finish --at R accepts that evaluation and appends its completion record together in one locked atomic transition only while the ledger head is still R. The resulting event is R+1 and explicitly certifies its parent R; it does not require evaluating itself. Any intervening record makes the submission stale. Non-final evaluation findings may be recorded normally, but cannot be reused to finish a later revision.
current.tradeoff: An unrelated intervening ledger record also requires re-evaluation; conservative freshness is preferable to extra version machinery at this scale.
current.revisit: Measured re-evaluation cost demonstrates a need to distinguish substantive changes from annotations.

current.question: How does new evidence reopen a completed task?
current.answer: After completion, reject ordinary mutations until an explicit reopen event cites the contradictory observation or reached revisit condition and names affected records. Append that event to the same history, invalidate affected dependents and prior completion, and return the same original design request to active status. Prior completion remains historical, never erased. Reopening grants no new authority. A materially different goal is a new task; changed intent or permissions must be sourced to the requester rather than inferred from reopening.
current.tradeoff: Reopening requires an explicit causal record; it preserves auditability without promising that all external contradictions can be detected automatically.
current.revisit: A real scope revision cannot be represented safely as either a requester-sourced revision or a separate task.

decisions.question: How should one CLI entry drive separate focused prompts?
decisions.answer: Use scripts/sbd.py --request TEXT to start, bare invocation to resume, and a printed done TICKET command to return a prompt result. A small code-owned router emits draft, resolve-one-need, or review prompts; resolve is optional and repeats only for a consequential need. Result validation, checkpoint and next prompt happen in the same call. Review pass publishes the current design and prints DONE. No workflow catalog, YAML or generic scheduler. This target is the adaptive repository, not the original skill used to run this design.
decisions.rationale: The request specifically replaces ledger-maintaining agent work with code-driven navigation and separate focused prompts.

decisions.question: What minimal checkpoint and completion contract replaces ledger mechanics?
decisions.answer: Keep one atomic current run snapshot: original request/constraints/permissions, current candidate, concise material basis/need, latest feedback, active prompt/ticket and status. No event history, evidence registry, question graph or per-record IDs. CLI-generated tickets and internal writer locking reject stale/concurrent results. Full redraft/review against the original request replaces dependency maintenance. Only passing review of the current candidate publishes an idempotent final artifact and returns DONE; publication errors never succeed. Blocked prompts resume with their current question. Explicit fresh requests start subsequent runs; old completed artifacts remain, legacy ledger state is not silently imported.
decisions.rationale: Interruption safety needs durable current context, not the old immutable history or dependency taxonomy. The original request remains available for every redraft/review.

decisions.tradeoff: Loses automatic transitive invalidation and machine-readable reasoning history; preserves final artifacts and rechecks the full current candidate. Review is local unless truly delegated; required independent review still blocks if unavailable.

decisions.question: How should migration and verification establish lower overhead without hiding regressions?
decisions.answer: Implement router/prompts first, then snapshot persistence and CLI, then trim entry/docs and remove ledger-only code/tests. Keep original skill and legacy task files unchanged; advertise the ledger API break, not a permanent compatibility mode. Test routing, prompt boundaries, normal-path calls, stale tickets, resume, corrupt state, concurrent writers and crash-safe publishing. Compare current/proposed instructions on the same model/tasks for trivial design, consequential intent, reversible choice, report-only authority, unsupported factual claim, material correction and blocked resumption. Measure procedural tokens/calls and consequential failures separately. Target >=70% median procedural-token reduction on that suite with no observed consequential regressions; claim no improvement before trials.
decisions.rationale: Existing ledger tests validate mechanics, not whether separate compact prompts improve actual adherence.

alternatives.option: Word counts and schema tests only
alternatives.rejected_because: Cannot establish adherence, honesty or requirement coverage.

alternatives.option: Keep two permanent runtimes for compatibility
alternatives.rejected_because: Adds concepts and maintenance contrary to the requested simplification.

decisions.tradeoff: A small matched suite provides limited evidence, not universal assurance; migration intentionally drops the old runtime API.

evidence.shows: Current tests encode ledger behavior; prior review disclaims measured behavioral improvement.
A practical adoption gate, not an observed improvement.

decisions.revisit: Trials show quality loss, insufficient overhead reduction or a necessary compatibility user.
